title: Penthouse Renderings Don't Sell One-Bedroom Units
seoTitle: Penthouse Renderings Don't Sell One-Bedroom Units
description: Using penthouse renderings to sell one-bedroom presale units creates doubt. Buyers need clarity on their own unit before they commit.
answer: Penthouse renderings set expectations that a one-bedroom unit cannot meet. When buyers of smaller units cannot see what they are buying, doubt drives their decision and sales slow down. Showing every unit in detail is what lets them close quickly.
body:
This is one of the most common problems I see when developers ask why a presale is slow.

## The standard approach

The project has a set of renderings. They are beautiful. They are almost always of the penthouse, or one of the best units, with the best view and the most space. Then the same images are used to sell every unit in the building.

## The disconnect

Now imagine you are buying a one-bedroom, one-bathroom unit on the fifth floor. You are shown a double-height living room with a panoramic view. You know that is not what you are getting. So what are you getting? Nobody shows you.

When buyers do not have clarity about their specific unit, everything feels a little uncertain. And when things feel uncertain, **fear drives the decision**. People wait, ask for more time, or walk away.

## You cannot render 350 units the traditional way

A developer with 350 units cannot commission 350 sets of traditional renderings. That is the reason most projects stop at a few hero images.

But technology has moved. Today it is possible to show every single unit, inch by inch, with its own layout and its own view.

## Clarity closes deals

When buyers understand exactly what they are buying, they decide quickly. The fastest way to sell the one-bedroom on the fifth floor is to show the one-bedroom on the fifth floor.
takeaways: Most presale renderings show the penthouse, not the units most people buy.
Buyers of smaller units feel the gap, and fear slows their decision.
Traditional renderings of every unit are too expensive for large projects.
Showing each unit in detail is what turns interest into fast decisions.
faq: Why do developers only render the penthouse?
Traditional renderings are costly, so developers render the most impressive units and amenities to make the project look its best.
How can a developer show every unit in a large project?
With digital tools that generate a walkthrough of each unit from the construction drawings, including its real layout and view.
Does seeing their unit really speed up sales?
Yes. Uncertainty about the unit is one of the main reasons buyers delay. Removing it shortens the time from interest to signature.
